Hi Mel, Thank you for your time.

In my words CP is price moving up with no pending buy limit order left below. Or price moving down with no pending sell limit order left above. Basically, it cleared the way for a possible quick moving back.

I have a few thought about CP, correct me if not right. 1. A bull flag on an up trend (in HTF) is a valid CP (in LTF). 2. A mild trend with a few deep enough pull backs is also a valid CP (in HTF). 3. CP doesn't tell which direction price will likely to go, it only tells if price moving back, it could be a quick big move.

Thanks in advance

UC

Nice explaination Ucego!

Cp is all about price taking the pockets of Supply (while going down)and the pockets of Demand (while going up) in order to clear the orders.

1)About your first point. I would say if you see compression on a higher TF, then you have CP on this timeframe. You can have cp on a higher TF and clean s/d levels on a small TF...

2) Yes, if you see that there was pockets of supply or demand where price pulled back.

3) You always have to look at the bigger picture that has been paint. I wouldn't look for cp just in the middle of a chart. If you see a clean fresh demand level and there is cp wile price goes down to this demand then this would be a very good sign of a potential reversal Up at the demand level.

However, if you see an unfresh demand level, that has been tested several times and you see cp while price goes down, you will still have to look at your chart to see if price will like to break the demand or just bounce back up.

But Cp is Cp... Price thinks ahead of time. If price cleared the pockets of supply while going down and price broke the demand than the cp that was made there will still be valid, only not for the imediate term but probably for later...

Best, Mel
